title: Running Java Applications in Production
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of running java applications in production and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—starting a jvm process—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study running java applications in production with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you prepare an artifact and runtime for observable, recoverable production operation. In this lesson, focus on starting a jvm process and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The JVM loads class files, verifies and executes bytecode, manages runtime memory, and may compile hot code for the host processor. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect starting a jvm process with runtime configuration before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Starting a JVM process
items.text: The JVM loads class files, verifies and executes bytecode, manages runtime memory, and may compile hot code for the host processor.

items.title: Runtime configuration
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.

items.title: Process lifecycle
items.text: Production readiness includes a reproducible artifact, explicit configuration, observability, graceful shutdown, compatibility checks, and a recovery plan—not just a successful local run. Apply that reasoning specifically to process lifecycle and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

items.title: Logging and diagnostics
items.text: Debug with a reproducible case, inspect a focused stack trace or state snapshot, and change one suspected cause at a time. Logs should support diagnosis without disclosing credentials or private data.

items.title: Graceful termination
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Keep runtime configuration outside source, document required environment values, and test graceful shutdown. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
